raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On integrated/unified-memory devices `get_available_gpu_memory()` reports
`psutil.virtual_memory().available` instead of the device pool, because
`torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` on those devices excludes reclaimable cache.
That value is not bounded by the device capacity: an APU whose GTT cap is
below the host RAM reports more available memory than the device can hold.

Measured on Ryzen AI MAX 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, ROCm 7.2.4):

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| `props.total_memory` | 108.0 GiB |
| `psutil.virtual_memory().available` | 122.08 GiB |
| `get_available_gpu_memory("cuda", 0)` | **122.08 GiB** |

The value feeds `pre_model_load_memory` and therefore the KV budget in
`_profile_available_bytes` (`rest ~= mem_fraction_static * pre - weights`).
`mem_fraction_static` is derived from the device capacity (108 GiB) while
`pre` comes from host availability (122 GiB), so the budget is inflated by
`mem_fraction_static * 14 GiB` and the pool request exceeds the device.

Reproduced with `sglang.launch_server` on Qwen3-0.6B with
`--mem-fraction-static 0.95 --attention-backend triton`
(decode/prefill CUDA graph disabled). Unpatched: the KV pool allocation dies
in `memory_pool.py` with
`HIP out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of
108.00 GiB of which 118.98 MiB is free. Of the allocated memory 107.58 GiB is
allocated by PyTorch`. The budget only stays inside the pool for the default
`mem_fraction_static` because of the slack; it breaks for
`mem_fraction_static >= capacity / host_available` (~0.885 here).

## Modifications

- Bound the integrated CUDA and MUSA branches by `props.total_memory`:
  `min(psutil.virtual_memory().available, props.total_memory)`.
- Keep the host-available metric (the reason it is used at all: `mem_get_info`
  excludes reclaimable cache and would under-report on Jetson-class devices),
  and only add the missing upper bound. When host availability is below the
  device total the returned value is unchanged.
- Cross-checked against the existing MPS precedent in the same function,
  which already bounds by `min(psutil.available, metal_headroom)`.
- Add hardware-free unit tests in `test/registered/unit/utils/test_common.py`
  covering host > total, host < total, and the discrete-device branch.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change only affects pool sizing, not model math.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed impact. Same launch config as above with the patch applied:

```
KV Cache is allocated. #tokens: 960570, K size: 51.30 GB, V size: 51.30 GB
Memory pool end. avail mem=14.59 GB
The server is fired up and ready to roll!
```

51.30 + 51.30 = 102.6 GiB = 108 GiB * 0.95, i.e. the budget is now derived
from the device capacity as intended, and the server starts instead of OOMing.
On the probe, `get_available_gpu_memory` returns 108.0 GiB instead of 122.08 GiB.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body: Checked the discrete-GPU side on RDNA3 (gfx1100, W7900-class, 48 GB): `is_integrated` is 0 there, so `get_available_gpu_memory` stays on the `mem_get_info` branch and this change does not affect it. That matters here because on this host `psutil.virtual_memory().available` is ~910 GiB, which would be badly wrong as a device budget. I have no APU to verify the integrated branch itself.

Thanks for checking the discrete side — and for flagging that you have no APU. I can fill that gap, since the integrated branch is exactly what this was measured on.

Host: Ryzen AI MAX 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, ROCm 7.2.4). `props.total_memory` = 108.0 GiB (GTT pool), host RAM 124.9 GiB, `psutil.virtual_memory().available` = 122.08 GiB, `is_integrated` = 1.

- Before the patch, `get_available_gpu_memory("cuda", 0)` returned **122.08 GiB**; after it returns **108.0 GiB**.
- Sanity check on the signal itself: `psutil.available` tracks GTT usage 1:1 here (122.08 -> 118.06 GiB after allocating 4 GiB), so the only defect was the missing upper bound, not the measurement.

Real failure on the unpatched build — `sglang.launch_server`, Qwen3-0.6B, `--mem-fraction-static 0.95 --attention-backend triton`, decode/prefill CUDA graphs disabled:

```
torch.OutOfMemoryError: HIP out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB. GPU 0 has a total
capacity of 108.00 GiB of which 118.98 MiB is free. Of the allocated memory 107.58 GiB
is allocated by PyTorch
```

at the KV pool allocation. The profiled budget was ~116 GiB, because `mem_fraction_static` is derived from the 108 GiB capacity while `pre_model_load_memory` came from the 122.08 GiB host figure. Same command with the patch:

```
KV Cache is allocated. #tokens: 960570, K size: 51.30 GB, V size: 51.30 GB
Memory pool end. avail mem=14.59 GB
The server is fired up and ready to roll!
```

51.30 + 51.30 = 102.6 GiB = 108 * 0.95, i.e. the budget is now derived from the device capacity. Unit tests: 3/3 pass patched; the `host availability > device total` case fails unpatched.

Your discrete result is what the code path implies: `is_integrated == 0` keeps `mem_get_info`, and `min()` only ever clips the integrated branch — on a 48 GB W7900 with ~910 GiB host-available RAM that is exactly why the cap must not apply there.

@@ -450,8 +450,10 @@ def get_available_gpu_memory(
             # On these devices, which use sysmem as device mem, torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
             # only reports "free" memory, which can be lower than what is actually
             # available due to not including cache memory. So we use the system available
-            # memory metric instead.
-            free_gpu_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().available
+            # memory metric instead. Host available memory can in turn exceed the device
+            # pool itself (e.g. an APU whose GTT cap is below the host RAM), which would
+            # size KV cache beyond what the device can hold, so bound it by the total.
+            free_gpu_memory = min(psutil.virtual_memory().available, props.total_memory)
         else:
             free_gpu_memory, _ = torch.cuda.mem_get_info(gpu_id)
 
@@ -533,8 +535,9 @@ def get_available_gpu_memory(
             # On these devices, which use sysmem as device mem, torch.musa.mem_get_info()
             # only reports "free" memory, which can be lower than what is actually
             # available due to not including cache memory. So we use the system available
-            # memory metric instead.
-            free_gpu_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().available
+            # memory metric instead, bounded by the device total for the same reason as
+            # in the CUDA branch above.
+            free_gpu_memory = min(psutil.virtual_memory().available, props.total_memory)
         else:
             free_gpu_memory, _ = torch.musa.mem_get_info(gpu_id)
     elif device == "mps":

@@ -13,6 +13,7 @@
     _load_image,
     flatten_arrays_to_int64_tensor,
     freeze_gc,
+    get_available_gpu_memory,
     get_device_sm_nvidia_smi,
     get_nvidia_driver_version_str,
 )
@@ -263,5 +264,69 @@ def test_applies_configured_threshold(self):
         self.assertEqual(gc.get_threshold(), (700, 10, 1000))
 
 
+class TestIntegratedDeviceAvailableMemory(CustomTestCase):
+    """Reported available memory must stay inside the device's own pool.
+
+    On unified-memory APUs (e.g. gfx1151 behind a GTT cap) the host can have
+    more RAM available than the device pool, so the raw psutil figure is e.g.
+    122 GiB on a 108 GiB device. That value feeds the KV cache budget, so it
+    is bounded by the device total instead.
+    """
+
+    TOTAL = 108 * (1 << 30)
+    HOST_AVAILABLE = 122 * (1 << 30)
+
+    def _call(self, *, available, total, is_integrated, mem_free):
+        props = mock.Mock(total_memory=total, is_integrated=is_integrated)
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(torch.cuda, "device_count", return_value=1),
+            mock.patch.object(torch.cuda, "current_device", return_value=0),
+            mock.patch.object(torch.cuda, "get_device_properties", return_value=props),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                torch.cuda, "mem_get_info", return_value=(mem_free, total)
+            ),
+            mock.patch(
+                "sglang.srt.utils.common.psutil.virtual_memory",
+                return_value=mock.Mock(available=available),
+            ),
+        ):
+            return get_available_gpu_memory("cuda", 0, empty_cache=False)
+
+    def test_host_availability_above_device_total_is_capped(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._call(
+                available=self.HOST_AVAILABLE,
+                total=self.TOTAL,
+                is_integrated=True,
+                mem_free=self.TOTAL,
+            ),
+            self.TOTAL / (1 << 30),
+        )
+
+    def test_host_availability_below_device_total_is_unchanged(self):
+        available = 40 * (1 << 30)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._call(
+                available=available,
+                total=self.TOTAL,
+                is_integrated=True,
+                mem_free=available,
+            ),
+            available / (1 << 30),
+        )
+
+    def test_discrete_device_ignores_host_availability(self):
+        free = 50 * (1 << 30)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._call(
+                available=self.HOST_AVAILABLE,
+                total=self.TOTAL,
+                is_integrated=False,
+                mem_free=free,
+            ),
+            free / (1 << 30),
+        )
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
